headline: Highest risk is low: no documented shared channels or writes, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are not evidenced for this pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared filesystem, clipboard, MCP server, or other ingestion path. agent_a has network_egress:none and agent_b also has network_egress:none, so there is no documented bridge for one agent’s outputs to hijack the other. The interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty is resolved conservatively but the pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not connect them through clipboard or shared message queues.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show network_egress:none. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, there is no plausible default path for sensitive data to flow from agent_a to agent_b or onward. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, this remains a docs-only assessment.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files or external egress, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of both agents’ working directories.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles expose no write surfaces, no filesystem permissions, and no network egress. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no documented capability conflict between agent_a and agent_b. Uncertainty is low because the relevant surfaces are empty in both profiles.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or shared mutable resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Avoid placing them in the same writable workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Neither profile documents output consumption, downstream action authority, or any parser that treats the other agent’s output as authoritative. agent_a is non-runnable and agent_b is a docs-backed library, so there is no evidenced execution chain where one agent’s output cascades into the other’s actions. The interaction is undocumented, so no default cascade is shown.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to execute actions from agent_a’s text without verification, cascading error risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated text.
Do not wire agent_a output directly into agent_b action prompts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. There is no documented residency, retention, or certification mismatch to evaluate, so no compliance breach is evidenced for this pair. Because only profile data is available, the absence of compliance-sensitive fields is decisive here.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document residency and retention before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy controls if regulated data is introduced.
